source.original_text: Faithful analytic-route paraphrase, not the full cited theorem: the PBPS Appendix C.1 argument uses conditional Gibbs Sobolev gradients, closedness and conditional Poincare. To apply a full-space weak-resolvent PDE route, the completed weighted smooth gradient must agree with an ordinary distributional gradient. For a strictly positive C1 Gibbs density exp(-W) with finite normalization, pairs (u,G) in the completed smooth compact gradient graph have locally volume-integrable representatives and satisfy integral psi inner(G,v) dx = -integral u D_v psi dx for compact C1 tests and constant v, with meaningful integrable test products. This follows by inserting exp(W)psi in the weighted identity and removing the weight locally. Kolesnikov-Milman1310.2526v7§2.5 supplies weighted Sobolev background, not an automatic transfer of compact-manifold regularity or spectral conclusions to Euclidean full space.

blind_reconstruction.text: For every type E equipped with a normed additive commutative group structure, a real inner-product-space structure, finite dimensionality over ℝ, and a measurable-space structure whose measurable sets are the Borel sets, and for every function W : E → ℝ, assume that W is continuously Fréchet differentiable and that x ↦ exp(-W(x)) is integrable with respect to volume on E. Let μ be volume tilted by the potential -W, namely the measure obtained by normalizing the density exp(-W) relative to volume. For every partial ℝ-linear map D from L²(μ; ℝ) to L²(μ; E), assume that D is closable and that, for every u ∈ L²(μ; ℝ) and G ∈ L²(μ; E), (u,G) belongs to the graph of D if and only if there exists a smooth function f : E → ℝ having compact support such that a chosen measurable representative of u equals f μ-almost everywhere and a chosen measurable representative of G equals ∇f μ-almost everywhere. Then, for every u ∈ L²(μ; ℝ) and G ∈ L²(μ; E) whose pair belongs to the graph of the closure of D, their chosen measurable representatives, denoted ũ : E → ℝ and G̃ : E → E, are both locally integrable with respect to volume. Furthermore, for every continuously Fréchet differentiable function ψ : E → ℝ having compact support and every vector v ∈ E, both functions x ↦ ψ(x)⟨G̃(x),v⟩ℝ and x ↦ ũ(x)(dψ(x))[v] are integrable with respect to volume, and ∫_E ψ(x)⟨G̃(x),v⟩ℝ dvol(x) = -∫_E ũ(x)(dψ(x))[v] dvol(x). Here dψ(x) is the real Fréchet derivative of ψ at x. This conclusion is only a forward implication from membership in the closed graph to the stated local integrability and distributional-gradient identity; no converse characterization of that graph is asserted.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.WeightedGradientWeak
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LocallyIntegrable

/-!
# Distributional meaning of the same weighted gradient closure

PBPS arXiv:2609.06905v1 Appendix C.1 analytic prerequisite, continuing the
weighted compact-test identity. Inverse positive Gibbs weights give local
volume integrability and genuine ordinary weak derivatives of L2 classes.
This is not the converse domain characterization, H2 regularity, an operator
core of D*D, a Poincare theorem or full paper completion.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.WeightedGradientDistribution

open MeasureTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace ContDiff Topology

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

private theorem lp_locallyIntegrable_volume {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
    [NormedSpace ℝ F] (W : E → ℝ) (hW : Continuous W)
    (hI : Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x)))
    (f : Lp F 2 ((volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x))) :
    LocallyIntegrable (fun x => f x) := by
  let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x)
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := isProbabilityMeasure_tilted hI
  have hi : Integrable (fun x => f x) μ :=
    MemLp.integrable (by norm_num : (1 : ENNReal) ≤ 2) (Lp.memLp f)
  have hr : Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) • f x) :=
    (integrable_tilted_iff hI _).mp hi
  have hl : LocallyIntegrable (fun x => Real.exp (W x) •
      (Real.exp (-W x) • f x)) (volume : Measure E) :=
    LocallyIntegrable.continuous_smul (μ := (volume : Measure E))
      (Real.continuous_exp.comp hW) hr.locallyIntegrable
  simpa only [smul_smul, ← Real.exp_add, add_neg_cancel, Real.exp_zero, one_smul] using hl

/-- Elements of the same closed weighted gradient graph have locally integrable
volume representatives and satisfy the ordinary weak gradient identity, with
both test products integrable. No differentiability of L2 representatives is
assumed, and no reverse characterization of the closure domain is asserted. -/
theorem closed_gradient_distributional (W : E → ℝ) (hW : ContDiff ℝ 1 W)
    (hI : Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x))) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x)
    ∀ (D : Lp ℝ 2 μ →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 μ), D.IsClosable →
      (∀ (u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) (G : Lp E 2 μ), (u,G) ∈ D.graph ↔
        ∃ f : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ f ∧ HasCompactSupport f ∧
          u =ᵐ[μ] f ∧ G =ᵐ[μ] gradient f) →
      ∀ (u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) (G : Lp E 2 μ), (u,G) ∈ D.closure.graph →
        LocallyIntegrable (fun x => u x) ∧ LocallyIntegrable (fun x => G x) ∧
        ∀ (ψ : E → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → ∀ v : E,
          Integrable (fun x => ψ x * inner ℝ (G x) v) ∧
          Integrable (fun x => u x * fderiv ℝ ψ x v) ∧
          (∫ x, ψ x * inner ℝ (G x) v) = - ∫ x, u x * fderiv ℝ ψ x v := by
  let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x)
  dsimp only
  intro D hD hgraph u G hu
  refine ⟨lp_locallyIntegrable_volume W hW.continuous hI u,
    lp_locallyIntegrable_volume W hW.continuous hI G, ?_⟩
  intro ψ hψ hc v
  let φ := fun x => Real.exp (W x) * ψ x
  have hφ : ContDiff ℝ 1 φ := hW.exp.mul hψ
  have hφc : HasCompactSupport φ := hc.mul_left
  have hq (x : E) : fderiv ℝ φ x v - φ x * fderiv ℝ W x v =
      Real.exp (W x) * fderiv ℝ ψ x v := by
    have hd := ((hW.differentiable one_ne_zero x).hasFDerivAt.exp).mul
      (hψ.differentiable one_ne_zero x).hasFDerivAt
    rw [show fderiv ℝ φ x = _ from hd.fderiv]
    simp only [add_apply, smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    dsimp [φ]
    ring
  have hcancel (x : E) : Real.exp (-W x) * Real.exp (W x) = 1 := by
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    simp
  have hl (x : E) : Real.exp (-W x) * (φ x * inner ℝ (G x) v) =
      ψ x * inner ℝ (G x) v := by
    dsimp only [φ]
    rw [← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, hcancel, one_mul]
  have hr (x : E) : Real.exp (-W x) *
      (u x * (fderiv ℝ φ x v - φ x * fderiv ℝ W x v)) = u x * fderiv ℝ ψ x v := by
    rw [hq]
    calc
      _ = (Real.exp (-W x) * Real.exp (W x)) * (u x * fderiv ℝ ψ x v) := by ring
      _ = _ := by rw [hcancel, one_mul]
  obtain ⟨hleft,hright,he⟩ := WeightedGradientWeak.closed_gradient_weighted_ibp
    W hW hI D hD hgraph u G hu φ hφ hφc v
  have hli := (integrable_tilted_iff hI _).mp hleft
  have hri := (integrable_tilted_iff hI _).mp hright
  simp only [smul_eq_mul, hl, hr] at hli hri
  refine ⟨hli,hri,?_⟩
  have ht (g : E → ℝ) : (∫ x, g x ∂μ) =
      (∫ x, Real.exp (-W x))⁻¹ * ∫ x, Real.exp (-W x) * g x := by
    rw [show μ = (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x) from rfl, integral_tilted]
    rw [← integral_const_mul]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [] with x
    change (Real.exp (-W x) / (∫ z, Real.exp (-W z))) • g x = _
    simp only [smul_eq_mul, div_eq_mul_inv]
    ring
  change (∫ x, φ x * inner ℝ (G x) v ∂μ) =
    -∫ x, u x * (fderiv ℝ φ x v - φ x * fderiv ℝ W x v) ∂μ at he
  rw [ht, ht] at he
  simp only [hl, hr, ← mul_neg] at he
  exact mul_left_cancel₀ (inv_ne_zero (integral_exp_pos hI).ne') he

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.WeightedGradientDistribution

For every ψ and v as above, both ψ⟨G,v⟩ and uD_vψ are volume-integrable, and their integrals have opposite signs. assumptions: E is any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. W:E→R is C1 and exp(-W) is integrable for Euclidean volume; μ=volume.tilted(-W) is the actual normalized Gibbs law.

D is a given closable partial real-linear map from scalar L²(μ) to vector L²(μ). Its original graph is exactly the pairs represented μ-almost everywhere by (f,∇f) for smooth compactly supported f. This is the interface already proved by WeightedGradient, not an assumed integration-by-parts formula.

Fix (u,G) in the graph of this same D.closure. Tests ψ are arbitrary C1 compact scalar functions, and v is any constant vector. The L2 coercions select measurable representatives; no differentiability, global volume integrability or tail bound for these representatives is assumed.

steps.title: Start with integrability for the Gibbs law
steps.text: For either scalar or vector representative h, finite μ makes L² membership imply L¹ membership. The actual tilted-measure integrability equivalence transfers this to integrability of e^(−W)h for volume. Positivity and finiteness of normalization follow from the assumed integrable exponential density.
steps.formula: h\in L^2(\mu)\Longrightarrow h\in L^1(\mu)\Longleftrightarrow e^{-W}h\in L^1(dx).

steps.title: Remove the weight locally
steps.text: Multiplication by a continuous scalar preserves local integrability. Apply this to e^W and the locally integrable e^(−W)h, then cancel exponentials. Doing this for both u and G establishes their local volume integrability without asserting global volume integrability.

steps.title: Choose the inverse-weighted test
steps.text: Given compact C1 ψ, set φ=e^Wψ. Continuity at infinity is irrelevant: its support stays inside the compact support of ψ, and φ is genuinely C1. Apply the existing weighted identity to the same D,u,G; no operator is replaced.

steps.title: Use the genuine first-order product rule
steps.text: Differentiate e^Wψ using the C1 hypotheses. Subtract φD_vW and cancel its two drift contributions. No classical derivative of u is used.

steps.title: Transfer both test-product integrabilities
steps.text: The parent proves both weighted products integrable under μ. Apply integrable_tilted_iff to each separately; multiply by e^(−W) and cancel e^(−W)e^W=1. These are actual volume-integrability proofs, not an appeal to the convention for undefined integrals.

steps.title: Cancel the positive normalization
steps.text: The tilted integral is Z⁻¹ times its density-weighted volume integral. Substitute the two pointwise cancellations into the parent identity and cancel Z⁻¹, which is nonzero. Together with local integrability this is the ordinary weak derivative identity, in one direction only.
